solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Book a restaurant within reach

definitions.meaning: to reserve a place to eat is to secure a spot at one, the three-word phrase
obtainable, able to be had, read as one hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A diner phoning ahead to reserve somewhere close by.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters split two ways: as a phrase (reserve somewhere to eat) and as a single adjective meaning obtainable.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserving at a restaurant is the everyday phrase; the hyphenated adjective means obtainable or reachable.

clue.text: Looked stunned as thong finally taken off

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word thong

parts.note: to take someone off is to mimic them, to ape

explanation.surface: Someone staring in shock as a thong is finally removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staring open-mouthed in amazement is a sign of being stunned.

clue.text: A personal detail another used to get you to pick up?

definitions.text: A personal detail another used to get you to pick up?

parts.words: A personal detail another used to get you to pick up?
parts.note: a personal detail that someone else dials so that you lift the receiver; pick up suggests a romantic pickup

explanation.surface: Someone using private information as a chat-up line.
explanation.definitionFit: The digits by which a caller reaches someone, getting them to answer the phone.

clue.text: Landlord about to declare payment going up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed payment wraps the word for declare
in a down answer going up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rent is the payment made to a landlord
to aver is to declare or assert

explanation.surface: A landlord about to announce that rent is rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' signals reading upwards in a down answer, which reverses the payment before it wraps the declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for one who keeps a tavern, a pub's landlord or innkeeper.

clue.text: Robber's group imprisoned?

indicators.note: the question mark flags that imprisoned works twice: it gives the bars and puts the group inside them

parts.note: imprisoned means behind bars, so the word bars stands for it
Abba was the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: Was a gang of thieves locked up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' does double duty: it supplies the bars and puts the pop group Abba behind them, so no single word is spare for a separate indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels he was the robber the crowd chose to free instead of Jesus, a prisoner awaiting execution.

clue.text: Puff perhaps, now apparently unhealthy?

definitions.meaning: a puff of breath is an example of breathing out
read as two parts, ex (formerly) and hale (healthy), so no longer healthy

explanation.surface: Smoking a cigarette, which now looks bad for health.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the split reading EX-HALE: formerly hale, so unhealthy now.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff is to blow breath out of the lungs.

clue.text: Gets less energy to contribute to enthusiasms

indicators.note: energy is added into the middle of the word for enthusiasms, contributing to it from inside

parts.note: fads are short-lived crazes or enthusiasms
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone running low on energy to put into their passions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dwindles or weakens gradually gets less, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Like some of Bach's music including runs, no way extravagant

indicators.note: including means the word holds another letter inside it

parts.note: Bach wrote many fugues, so some of his music is fugal
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Bach's music with its scale runs is far from showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrifty and sparing with money, the opposite of lavish spending.

clue.text: Killer of wife smiled wickedly in repose

parts.note: dutch is Cockney slang for a wife, from duchess

indicators.note: wickedly suggests going astray, so the letters of smiled are rearranged

parts.note: ease is a state of rest or repose

explanation.surface: A murderer of his wife who smirked as he rested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' for wife comes from Cockney 'duchess' ('my old Dutch'). 'wickedly' turns SMILED into ELMDIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal blight that killed most of Britain's elm trees in the 1970s.

clue.text: A little light covering garden may in the end become inactive

indicators.note: the word for light goes over and around the garden, covering it

parts.note: a star is a small point of light in the sky
Eden was the biblical garden

indicators.note: in the end points to the last letter of may

explanation.surface: A garden lamp may eventually stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is just a link; the light is split open by the garden rather than sitting beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting a lot and taking little exercise, so physically idle.

clue.text: Lighter verse included after a discussion

indicators.note: the pair of a and verse go inside the word for lighter, held within it

parts.note: paler means lighter in colour

indicators.note: verse is placed after a, so the pair reads A then V

explanation.surface: Light verse being added to something after a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts AV inside PALER, splitting it as PAL-AV-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, fussy and often pointless discussion or rigmarole; the word came into English from Portuguese for talk.

clue.text: Man had to welcome relative that's regularly visited

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so the relative goes inside the other letters

parts.note: he'd is a contraction of he had, man giving he
an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A man who took in a family member, now a frequent visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man had' is the contraction he'd, with its apostrophe ignored as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A place visited regularly, especially by a ghost, is said to be haunted; also frequented.

clue.text: Con man's very fine, getting rid of policeman

indicators.note: getting rid of means one part of the longer word is taken away

parts.note: super-duper is slang for excellent or very fine
super is short for superintendent, a senior police officer

explanation.surface: A swindler claims to be doing splendidly now the copper has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: From the rhyming phrase for very fine, remove its first half, the police superintendent.
explanation.definitionFit: One who dupes or deceives others is a swindler or trickster.

clue.text: A feature on plain canopy

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means coming after, so a feature follows plain

parts.note: bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A plain canopy with a single decorative element.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial canopy over an altar, throne or bed, often of rich fabric, is called by this term.

clue.text: Dictionaries include papyrus here, at a premium

definitions.meaning: in alphabetical order the headword papyrus comes before, so is printed higher than, the word par
selling for more than the face value

explanation.surface: Dictionaries that include papyrus are sought after.
explanation.walkthrough: PAP comes before PAR alphabetically, so in a dictionary papyrus sits higher on the page than par.
explanation.definitionFit: A share trading at a premium is priced higher than its nominal value.

clue.text: Car pool is relocated in classical site

indicators.note: relocated means moved to new places, so these letters change position

explanation.surface: A car-sharing scheme moved to an ancient location.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens's hilltop citadel holding the Parthenon is the best-known ancient Greek monument complex.

clue.text: Russian family always is accommodating

indicators.note: the phrase holds a run of letters inside it, as a house accommodates a guest

explanation.surface: A Russian family that always puts people up.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Russian given name, as for the composer Glinka's or novelist Ehrenburg's, so a Russian man.

clue.text: Skyline against one lake

parts.note: contra is Latin for against
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A view of the horizon set against a single lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skyline' looks like the horizon, but here it is a line in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A vapour trail left by an aircraft is literally a line drawn across the sky.

clue.text: Sort of prison, basic, not one without walls

parts.note: an open prison has minimal security

indicators.note: not one means the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: plain means simple or basic
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A basic jail with no walls at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A layout with no internal partitions dividing the space, as in modern offices.

clue.text: For audience interpret oboe part

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard by listeners, a word that sounds like another

parts.note: to read is to interpret, as reading a situation

explanation.surface: An oboe player interpreting their part for listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe's sound comes from a double reed, a vibrating piece of cane in its mouthpiece.

clue.text: Dad and when he's remunerated: not a charitable occasion

parts.note: pop is an informal name for father

indicators.note: not a means the letter a is taken out of the word before it

parts.note: payday is the day workers are paid

explanation.surface: Dad's payday is not a charitable occasion, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The British day of selling poppies for the Royal British Legion, around Remembrance Day in November.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the annual fundraising day for veterans' charity, when paper poppies are sold.

clue.text: Cowcatcher in car, not the front, in the flipping rear!

indicators.note: the trimmed car sits inside the reversed word for rear
flipping means turned over, so the word for rear is read backwards

parts.note: the tail is the rear end

indicators.note: not the front means the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A cowboy's rope in the back of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowcatcher' suggests the grille on a locomotive, but here it is a cowboy's rope. 'flipping' gives LIAT; AR goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a noose used for catching cattle.

clue.text: Curly marks, first piece of decoration in mosaic

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the word for mosaic

parts.note: a mosaic is made of small tiles

indicators.note: first piece means just the opening letter

explanation.surface: Decorative curls set in a mosaic floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy accent mark, as over the n in Spanish words, is a curly sign.

clue.text: Resenter of taxes paid nothing, just furious

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A taxpayer angrily claims to have paid nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A follower of Pierre Poujade, who led a 1950s French protest movement of small shopkeepers against taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement was famous for opposing taxes, so a follower is a resenter of them.

clue.text: Sounding affected by cold, maybe left a clinic from the back

indicators.note: reading from the back means taking the letters in backwards order

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a clinic

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold leaving a clinic by the rear door.
explanation.definitionFit: A blocked nose gives the voice a nasal, through-the-nose quality.

clue.text: Composer tending to relax you?

definitions.meaning: Jean-Baptiste ..., the Italian-born French Baroque composer at the court of Louis XIV
a made-up adjective from lull, soothing, like a lullaby

explanation.surface: A composer whose music soothes the listener.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Lully was the leading court composer to Louis XIV and founder of French opera.

clue.text: Tried to influence lout, one not up yet?

parts.note: lob is an old dialect word for a lout or clumsy fellow
one not up yet is I still in bed, so I sits inside BED

explanation.surface: Pressuring a layabout who has not got out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a little picture: one (I) not yet up is in BED, giving B-I-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to press politicians or officials to support a cause.

clue.text: Nothing but a drop of the hard stuff that may greet one

parts.note: all means nothing but, as in all talk

parts.words: a drop of the hard stuff
parts.note: hail is frozen precipitation, a hard drop rather than a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone offered just a nip of whisky as a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard stuff' suggests spirits, but here it is ice falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional exclamation of welcome or acclamation, as said to a king or hero.

clue.text: Peacock's extremely short mating period

indicators.note: taking a word at its extremes gives its first and last letters

parts.note: the rut is the breeding season of deer and similar animals

explanation.surface: A peacock has a very brief breeding season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peacock' is a verb here: to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: To peacock is to parade about vainly, the same as swaggering along proudly.

clue.text: Notice about temperature in ship dangerous to hands?

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for notice wraps the rest

parts.note: to spy is to notice or catch sight of

indicators.note: in places temperature inside the word for ship

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Seeing the thermometer reading on board a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes LINTER, a container nested inside another container.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough wood full of splinters can pierce the skin of anyone handling it.
